10   Q        PLEASE SUMMARIZE YOUR FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS.

11   A        My findings and recommendations are as follows:

12            Deferred Tax Asset
13             •    SPS requests approval to recover a return on the deferred tax asset (DTA)
14                  created by the sale of production tax credits (PTCs) associated with Plant X
15                  Solar, Cunningham I Solar, and Cunningham II Solar projects (collectively, the
16                  SPS Solar Projects). The Company proposes to recover the return on the
17                  DTA through the Fuel and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause
18                  (FPPCAC) and earn a return on the average monthly balance of the DTA at
19                  its requested weighted average cost of capital (WACC) or 8.21%.1
20             •    SPS should earn a return at its short-term cost of debt, not its WACC.
21             •    The return on the DTA should not be recovered in the FPPCAC, it should be
22                  recovered in base rates, as authorized in Case No. 25-00270-UT.

23            Investment Tax Credits and Transfer Costs
24             •    SPS also requests approval to book the investment tax credits (ITCs)
25                  associated with the Cunningham 1 battery energy storage system (BESS) and
26                  Plant X BESS as a regulatory liability, amortize the value over five years, and
27                  to book costs associated with the transfer of the ITCs as a regulatory asset.

13             funds related to the ITC in one lump sum payment — as such, there is no reason why

20             transfer the ITC in August 2027.9 It is appropriate to use SPS’s long-term cost of debt

12   Deferral Mechanisms
13   Q    PLEASE      DESCRIBE       SPS’S      PROPOSED       REGULATORY           ACCOUNTING

14        DEFERRALS.

15   A    SPS is seeking approval for the continuation of several regulatory accounting orders,

16        as well as approval for two new deferral mechanisms. The proposals are:

17         •   Continue the deferral mechanism to track expenses associated with ELI
18             expense;
19         •   Continuation of the deferral for its investment in legacy meters;
20         •   Continuation of the deferral account for Community Solar and information
21             technology costs;
22         •   A property tax tracker; and
23         •   A deferral mechanism to track any SPP deficiency payments.

24        As discussed more fully below, deferral mechanisms are a form of piecemeal

25        ratemaking and should be rejected.

 1   Q   DO YOU HAVE ANY CONCERNS RELATING TO SPS’S CURRENT AND

 2       PROPOSED REGULATORY ACCOUNTING DEFERRALS?

 3   A   Yes. SPS is seeking to recover the exact amount of expenses for these regulatory

 4       accounts, while also using a fully projected future test year. SPS chose to use a future

 5       test year, therefore, its projected costs for these regulatory deferrals should be

 6       included in rates and not tracked. SPS has presumably chosen a fully projected future

 7       test year because it will improve its financial condition as it reduces regulatory lag (and

 8       shifts risk onto SPS’s customers). If a projected future test year accurately predicts

 9       costs and sales for future periods, then it should not also be necessary to have

10       regulatory accounting deferrals. SPS wants the benefit of both a fully projected future

11       test year and regulatory accounting deferrals. It cannot have it both ways. A projected

12       future test year negates the need for accounting deferrals.


13   Q   WHAT IS PIECEMEAL RATEMAKING?

14   A   Piecemeal ratemaking occurs when rates change outside of a base rate case to reflect

15       only one factor without also recognizing other factors that offset any increase or

16       decrease in rates. This Commission has a longstanding policy against piecemeal

17       ratemaking, which it has had for decades.


18   Q   HOW SHOULD THE COMMISSION TREAT SPS’S REQUESTS FOR DEFERRED

19       ACCOUNTING?

20   A   Consistent with Commission precedent, the Commission should reject SPS’s attempts

21       to engage in piecemeal ratemaking through deferral requests. Deferral accounting

22       fails to take into account any increased revenues or expense savings that would offset

23       the increase in deferred expenses.

 1   Q   ARE THERE ANY OTHER REASONS WHY THE COMMISSION SHOULD REJECT

 2       SPS’S REQUESTS TO CONTINUE ITS CURRENTLY AUTHORIZED DEFERRAL

 3       MECHANISM?

 4   A   Yes.   First, as mentioned above, extending the deferral mechanisms represents

 5       piecemeal ratemaking. Second, any change in the costs related to the current deferral

 6       mechanisms is reflected in the proposed rates in this case. Therefore, there is no

 7       need to continue to defer the ELI expense.


 8   Q   SHOULD SPS BE ALLOWED TO DEFER SOUTHWEST POWER POOL

 9       DEFICIENCY PAYMENTS?

10   A   No. First, Ms. Lees states “SPS is evaluating other options, including short-term

11       capacity purchases, but at this point SPS anticipates it will be required to make a

12       deficiency payment.” Because it isn’t clear at this time whether SPS will purchase

13       short-term capacity, or if it must pay deficiency payments, it is premature for SPS to

14       seek recovery of deficiency payments in the FPPCAC.             Second, if SPS incurs

15       additional costs related to a capacity shortfall it may seek recovery of those costs in a

16       future proceeding.


17   Q   IF   THE   COMMISSION        AUTHORIZES         SPS   TO    RECOVER       DEFICIENCY

18       PAYMENTS, SHOULD THEY BE RECOVERED IN THE FPPCAC?

19   A   No. The FPPCAC is designed to recover fuel and purchased power expense, which

20       is incurred on a per kilowatt-hour basis. The SPP deficiency payments are related to

21       capacity shortfalls. Accordingly, if SPS were to recover the SPP deficiency payments,

22       they should be through base rates and not in the FPPCAC.
